lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 82, which opens Thunar's rename box in a popover right next to the file.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request eighty-two, which opens Thunar's rename box in a popover right next to the file.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
You press F2, or choose Rename, on one selected file.
Thunar finds the file's row, scrolls it into view if needed, and takes its Name cell.
The popover opens below the name, or above it near the bottom, sized to fit the name.
Enter renames the file; Escape or a click outside cancels.
For a launcher file, the launcher-or-file question now opens over the Thunar window.
A rename asked for over D-Bus has no view to point at, so it keeps the dialog, now over a Thunar window.
lines.say: A rename asked for over D Bus has no view to point at, so it keeps the dialog, now over a Thunar window.

lines.caption: The old dialog had no parent window, so it often opened on another monitor, and it never grew past 500 pixels.
lines.say: The old dialog had no parent window, so it often opened on another monitor, and it never grew past five hundred pixels.

lines.caption: A popover is drawn inside its window, so it can't land on another monitor.
The window's action manager now passes its current view, so the rename knows where the file is shown.
The details view returns the row's Name cell; the icon and compact views point at their middle for now.
The popover holds the same icon, entry and buttons as the dialog, between 300 pixels and 90 percent of the window.
lines.say: The popover holds the same icon, entry and buttons as the dialog, between three hundred pixels and ninety percent of the window.

lines.caption: The name is selected without its extension, and the focus goes back to the file list afterwards.
The launcher question and the D-Bus dialog are now tied to the Thunar window.
lines.say: The launcher question and the D Bus dialog are now tied to the Thunar window.

lines.caption: Only renames from a view get the popover; the side pane, the location bar and D-Bus keep the dialog.
lines.say: Only renames from a view get the popover; the side pane, the location bar and D Bus keep the dialog.

lines.caption: Most of the change is in the dialogs file, with small additions to the views, the window and the application.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It reuses the old dialog's content, waits the way the dialog did, and finds the row the way the views already do.
The package was built in this session.
The test showed the popover below a top row and above the last one, and the extension left unselected.
Escape, a click outside and an invalid name left the file alone, and hidden rows scrolled into view.
Long names, the icon and compact views, the launcher question and the D-Bus dialog were checked too.
lines.say: Long names, the icon and compact views, the launcher question and the D Bus dialog were checked too.

lines.caption: The whole sandbox test set was run on the last code change.
A second monitor and a two-thousand-pixel window couldn't be tested here.
A fresh review agent found one medium and two low problems, and all three were fixed.
The medium one: pressing F2 twice stacked a second popover. A second F2 is now ignored.
After the merge, you can check the second monitor, a wide window, and the split-view crash.
Part 3. What comes later: in-place rename, issue 16.
lines.say: Part 3. What comes later: in-place rename, issue sixteen.

lines.caption: After your check, issue 16 adds renaming right in the list, with this popover as its fallback.
lines.say: After your check, issue sixteen adds renaming right in the list, with this popover as its fallback.

lines.caption: With its new preference off, F2 opens this popover, and launchers and D-Bus keep their windows.
lines.say: With its new preference off, F2 opens this popover, and launchers and D Bus keep their windows.

lines.caption: In short: the rename box now opens next to the file, on the right monitor, and wide enough for the whole name.
